summary: NDR feed s051_single is degraded: 32.2% of TCP sessions (68/211) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. NDR requires bidirectional traffic for session reassembly. All other visibility checks (duplicates, drops, overload, VLAN, encryption) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is delivering only one direction for many flows. Most likely cause is SPAN configured to mirror Tx or Rx only, single-sided TAP placement on asymmetric routed path, or broker not aggregating both directions of a flow to the same NDR tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs_both_directions=true and needs_full_payload=true. With 32.2% one-way sessions it cannot reassemble TCP, track state, or correlate request/response, causing missed detections, broken flow records, and reduced detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same 10G NDR port with flow-aware affinity so the NDR sees complete bidirectional sessions. If current source is SPAN, replace with TAP-based aggregation to avoid SPAN directional/mirroring gaps.
